---
title: "Beyond the Mean Field"
description: "When one averaged unit per region is not enough: spiking cells, ion channels and multi-scale models."
---

Most TVB-O models put a single averaged unit at each region. That is the right level for whole-brain dynamics, and the wrong one as soon as the question turns on individual spikes, a specific ion channel, or what a detailed patch does inside an otherwise coarse brain.

Two escapes exist, and they answer different questions.

**Reference a detailed cell model.** Single neurons, ion channels and synapses are available by IRI: set `iri: neuroml:<TypeName>` on a dynamics and TVB-O pulls the equations from the NeuroML2 library rather than making you transcribe them. See [IRI vs. inline YAML](../Interoperability/NeuroML/IRI_vs_YAML.qmd) and the [example gallery](../Interoperability/NeuroML/examples/index.qmd).

**Run two scales together.** [Multi-scale modelling](MultiScaleModelling.qmd) covers what it means to couple a detailed patch to a whole-brain model, which pairings TVB-O supports today, and an honest status for each. Not every combination works yet, and that page says which.

The macro network a detailed patch attaches to is specified the ordinary way, in [Networks & connectomes](../Networks/index.qmd).
